A window plant has one leaf covered so no light reaches it, the other leaves are in the light, and the soil is watered.

nodes.text: The plant with one covered leaf

Here is a healthy plant in a window. It is watered as usual. One leaf has a cover on it, and the cover keeps light out. The other leaves stay uncovered in the light. Look at the covered leaf. Do you think that leaf can still make food? Say what you think, and give a reason for your answer.

A leaf needs light to make food. On the window plant, the cover over one leaf comes first: because of the cover, light no longer reaches that leaf. The uncovered leaves still receive light, so they can make food. But with light blocked from the covered leaf, that one leaf cannot make food — even though the plant is watered as usual. Water stays the same for every leaf, so the cover and the blocked light, not water, are what explain why the covered leaf cannot make food.

nodes.caption: A watered plant in a window. Light falls on the uncovered leaves, so they can make food. The cover over one leaf stops light from reaching it, so that leaf cannot make food.
nodes.alt: A potted plant standing in a window, watered as usual. Light from the window shines on the uncovered leaves, which can make food. One leaf is enclosed in a cover; light is shown stopping at the cover, so that leaf receives no light and cannot make food. The water in the pot is unchanged throughout.

nodes.title: The idea the case turns on
nodes.body: A leaf with a cover over it gets no light, and without light a leaf cannot make food. The water the plant receives does not change that.

nodes.text: Explaining the covered leaf on the watered plant
Think back to the plant in the window: one leaf was covered, the other leaves were left in the light, and the soil was watered. Choose the explanation that follows from the chain you traced.

nodes.prompt: Look at the plant in the window. It is watered as usual, one leaf is wrapped in a cover that keeps light out, and the other leaves are uncovered in the light. Do you think the covered leaf can still make food, and why?

options.text: No, because the cover keeps light from reaching that leaf
options.explanation: This does not match the stateable belief that coverage blocks light from the leaf.

options.text: Yes, because the plant is watered as usual
options.explanation: Names the misconception that water alone is enough for a leaf to make food.

options.text: Yes, because the rest of the plant looks healthy
options.explanation: Names the misconception that one leaf's food-making can be inferred from the plant's overall appearance.

nodes.prompt: A window plant has one leaf covered so no light reaches it, the other leaves are in the light, and the soil is watered. Why will the covered leaf be unable to make food?

options.text: The cover stops light reaching that leaf, and a leaf needs light to make food.
options.explanation: Correct: this follows the chain that light is needed to make food and the cover blocks light.

options.text: Because the plant was not watered enough.
options.explanation: Misses the mechanism: the soil is watered, so lack of water is not the cause.

options.text: Because water is what makes food, and the leaf got none.
options.explanation: Reveals the misconception that water itself makes food rather than supplying materials.

feedback.correct: Yes. The cover blocks light to that leaf, and light is needed to make food, so the water the plant gets cannot replace the missing light.
feedback.incorrect: Look again at the covered leaf: the soil is watered, so the problem is not water. The cover stops light reaching that leaf, and light is needed to make food.
